newsitem.title: USA: Train carrying chemicals derailed in Arizona.
newsitem.headline: Train carrying chemicals derailed in Arizona.

text.p: Cars from an Apache Railway freight train that may be carrying hazardous chemicals derailed in northeastern Arizona Monday, forcing the evacuation of about 150 nearby residents, authorities said.
Law enforcement officials at the scene said there were no injuries reported, but that one of the runaway cars burst into flames and was still burning late Monday night in Holbrook, Ariz.
Officials were trying to determine what if any hazardous chemicals were involved in the incident, according to Jerry Wyatt, the city's emergency service coordinator.
Wyatt estimated that about 25 rail cars jumped the tracks at 7:50 p.m. MST in a rural area in the south portion of the small community, about 200 miles northeast of Phoenix.
Area residents were evacuated to a local church and high school gymnasium as a precaution. In addition, a local Seventh Day Adventist boarding school also was evacuated.
"We're not sure what we're dealing with right now so we wanted to do all we could to make sure that everyone is safe," Wyatt said. "That's what's most important."
Authorities could not immediately determine why the cars had derailed.
